items.title: Lua 5.5
items.raw_content: Here is a chronology of the versions of Lua. The evolution of Lua is documented in a paper presented at HOPL III, the Third ACM SIGPLAN History of Programming Languages Conference , in 2007. See also its continuation published in 2025 in a journal . The source code and documentation for all releases of Lua are available in the download area . The source code of recent releases is also available for browsing . Numbering scheme The releases of Lua are numbered x.y.z , where x is the series, x.y is the version, and z is the release. This scheme superficially resembles the popular semantic versioning scheme but is not the same, especially regarding compatibility. Here are the details. Different releases of the same version correspond to bug fixes ; they have the same reference manual , the same virtual machine, and are binary compatible (ABI compatible). items.title: NIST was 5 μs off UTC after last week's power cut
items.raw_content: If you were 5 microseconds late today, blame it on NIST. Their facility in Boulder Colorado just had its power cut for multiple days. After a backup generator failed, their main ensemble clock lost track of UTC, or Universal Time Coordinated. But even if you used the NTP timing servers they run, they were never off by more than 5 microseconds. 5 Î¼s might seem insignificant. But it is significant for scientists and universities who rely on NIST's more specialized timing signals.
items.title_zh: 上周停电后 NIST 与 UTC 偏差达 5 微秒
items.summary: After a multi-day power cut at NIST's Boulder, Colorado facility and the failure of a backup generator, its main ensemble clock lost track of UTC, though its NTP servers were never off by more than 5 microseconds.

items.title: The Garbage Collection Handbook
items.raw_content: Richard Jonesâs Garbage Collection (Wiley, 1996) was a milestone book in the area of automatic memory management. Its widely acclaimed successor, The Garbage Collection Handbook: The Art of Automatic Memory Management captured the state of the field in 2012. However, technology developments have made memory management more challenging, interesting and important than ever. This second edition updates the handbook, bringing together a wealth of knowledge gathered by automatic memory management researchers and developers over the past sixty years. The authors compare the most important approaches and state-of-the-art techniques in a single, accessible framework.
